title: Practice Makes Precise: At CoRL, NVIDIA and Partners Reveal How Robots Rehearse Delicate Work in Simulation
body: Practice Makes Precise: At CoRL, NVIDIA and Partners Reveal How Robots Rehearse Delicate Work in Simulation At the Conference on Robot Learning, NVIDIA is introducing GR00T 2, Isaac Lab 3.0 and new open benchmarks, built in collaboration with partners, bringing precision and scale to robot training. November 9, 2026 by Sasa Docca 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Simulation, which has long been the proving ground for robots learning to walk, roll and hop, is now helping researchers teach robots tasks that require a finer touch: aligning gears, connecting cables and assembling small components. The shift from locomotion to manipulation is taking center stage at this week’s Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL) in Austin, Texas, alongside the rise of agentic robotics — a new paradigm that integrates frontier agents to create interpretable code for physical robotics systems. At CoRL, NVIDIA is introducing new open robotics technologies, including world action models , simulation tools, benchmarks and agentic workflows. Two NVIDIA papers are among six finalists out of thousands of submissions for the Best Paper Awards at CoRL: GRAIL (Generating Humanoid Loco-Manipulation from World Models), which presents a digital generation pipeline for 3D assets and simulator-ready scenes for robot learning. RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies , which introduces a robot model and training recipe that scales visuomotor context three orders of magnitude beyond state-of-the-art policies without growing inference latency. These advancements help researchers train robots on complex tasks, evaluate their performance across changing conditions and use failures to guide further learning — building the precision, adaptability and autonomy needed to move from lab demonstrations to industrial deployment. NVIDIA is working with partners like Ambi Robotics , Bosch Research , Dexmate , Dyna Robotics , FieldAI , Flexion , Noitom Robotics , Siemens , Skild AI , RLWRLD , UC Berkeley , Walden Robotics and the University of Washington to bring these advancements to the broader robotics community. World Action Models Enable Next Level of Robot Autonomy The next level of robot autonomy requires robots to perceive their surroundings, anticipate how their actions will change the environment and execute complex, multistep tasks with a high degree of precision. World action models enable exactly that. At CoRL, NVIDIA is introducing GR00T 2 , an open frontier world action model built on NVIDIA Cosmos. Trained on diverse robot and human data, including 100,000 hours of NVIDIA open source human egocentric data , the model enables robots to learn dexterous manipulation skills. Key features include: Out-of-the-box performance: Completed 40 of 50 evaluated tasks at least once without task-specific demonstrations. Skill transfer: Learns from human demonstrations and transfers skills between different robot bodies without robot demonstrations Generalization with little data: Achieved 71% average success across 50 tasks with just one demonstration per task, increasing to 95% with five. Agent control: AI agents can use GR00T 2’s application programming interface and supporting tools to run skills in sequence and recover from errors. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/groot-2-shipping-label.mp4 GR00T 2 currently ranks among the top three models across all vision language action and world action model categories for the RoboCasa365, RoboLab, RoboDojo and MolmoSpaces benchmarks, with multiple leaderboard wins. Nexuni is testing it for robotic laundry handling, Foxconn is applying GR00T 2 to factory automation for server manufacturing and Siemens is evaluating it across industrial use cases. MicroAGI is using GR00T 2, post-trained through reinforcement learning, to perform Ethernet cable swapping with a YAM robotic arm. Its agentic robotics approach automates the creation and calibration of simulation environments using Isaac Lab 3.0 and Newton, where the policy is trained. The agentic robotics workflow will be demonstrated at CoRL. Training capable robots requires diverse data. Open NVIDIA workflows and models equip researchers with better tools for data collection and annotation: For researchers building robot-training datasets, NVIDIA’s new open Video to Data workflow turns human video into simulated robot demonstrations, with a challenge inviting researchers to advance it. The NVIDIA EgoHand open model — being demoed at CoRL and with over 40,000 Hugging Face downloads in the two weeks since launch — reconstructs 3D hand motion, trained with data from Noitom Robotics . https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/egohand-demo.mp4 Where the Training and Scaling Happens — in Simulation A pretrained model gives robots a core set of skills. Simulation lets researchers train, refine and evaluate skills at scale before deploying them on physical robots. NVIDIA Isaac Lab , an open source robot-learning framework, provides the foundation for that work. Its latest release, Isaac Lab 3.0 , allows researchers to use agents to quickly set up training environments with simulation-ready assets , switch between NVIDIA PhysX and Newton physics solvers , choose renderers for perception-based training and apply a new reinforcement post-training library to foundation models like GR00T. Accurate physics is critical to transferring learned skills from simulation to the real robot. Tighter integration with Newton , an open source physics engine, now allows Isaac Lab to model deformable objects such as cables and cloth, along with complex articulated systems such as robotic hands with many interacting joints. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/newton-strawberry.mp4 Integration with Newton simulates how a strawberry deforms under a robot’s grip. Together, Isaac Lab and Newton combine accurate physics with scale to enable researchers to train thousands of simulated robots in parallel. In a vision-based dexterous manipulation benchmark, Isaac Lab 3.0 with Newton achieved up to 2.5x the training throughput of Isaac Lab 2.3 with PhysX. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/newton-physx-web.mp4 Isaac Lab supports robot simulation with Newton and NVIDIA PhysX. Developers are extending Newton’s capabilities. At CoRL, Skild AI announced Scalable Throughput-optimized Engine for Embodied Learning, or STEEL, a new rigid-body physics solver built on Newton to accelerate robot training with Isaac Lab. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/robotics-montage-8s.mp4 Skild AI’s STEEL Solver. Flexion showcased how Isaac Lab and Newton help train Reflect, its robot-intelligence model combining reasoning and whole-body manipulation. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/flexion-newton-isaac-lab.mp4 Flexion uses Newton for RL with Isaac Lab. FieldAI is using Newton — as well as Isaac Lab and Isaac Sim, built on NVIDIA Omniverse libraries — to train and validate robot policies for deployment in unstructured real-world environments. Dyna Robotics will demonstrate how parallel simulation in Isaac Lab helps train whole-body controllers for its semi-humanoid Taku robot for work in warehouses, hotels and food services. Walden Robotics is using Isaac Sim’s photorealistic rendering to train and evaluate its general-purpose robot in virtual environments for manufacturing and logistics, while Dexmate is exploring how coding agents can rehearse and refine manipulation strategies in Isaac Sim before executing them on its Vega robot. AlphaNIST , built in Isaac Lab, demonstrates how efficient practice can translate into precision. A single policy learns all 20 tasks on the NIST Assembly Task Board, manipulating  millimeter-scale parts using only a yes-or-no success signal. It achieves more than 98% training success, compared with 81% for separate per-task policies, using roughly 39x less GPU time. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/alphanist-6-16s-web.mp4 AlphaNIST uses Isaac Lab to train a single robot policy across 20 precision tasks on the NIST Assembly Task Board. Behind those results is Success-Guided Sampling , or SGS, from the University of Washington and NVIDIA. The method focuses practice on tasks a policy succeeds at about half the time, directing training toward skills it’s still learning. With SGS, robot training can scale beyond a million parallel environments. The University of Texas at Austin’s School of Computing and Texas Robotics uses Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab to train robotic skills in simulation, letting students start developing before physical hardware is available. New Industrial Benchmarks for Robot Evaluation Learning a skill is one challenge. Performing it reliably across changing conditions is another. NVIDIA Isaac Lab-Arena , an open source framework for scaled policy evaluation, enables developers to compose diverse and repeatable evaluations, then run policies across thousands of variations in parallel. Analyses expose which conditions cause failures, so researchers know what to fix in their next training run. The developer preview of its latest version, 0.4, is arriving at CoRL. DexBench and VABAR, two new open benchmarks, are among the first designed to measure robot dexterity and adaptability across industrial tasks using Isaac Lab-Arena and Newton. DexBench , developed by RLWRLD in collaboration with NVIDIA, takes dexterity evaluation off the tabletop and into real-world workflows. Built using NVIDIA Isaac Lab-Arena, it features 15 tasks across four scenes spanning retail, logistics, manufacturing and hospitality, testing generalization across object, spatial and physics variations. Genesis AI , mimic robotics and other industry partners are evaluating DexBench through early access. Teams can run DexBench on Manifold, Bifrost’s evaluation platform for scaling robotics simulations, with no setup required, built-in failure analysis and free credits for initial evaluations. VABAR — the Variational Automation Benchmark for Agentic Robotics — from UC Berkeley and NVIDIA, evaluates robots across six industrial tasks. Each carries standardized variations, difficulty tiers and success metrics. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/task-tool-sorting.mp4 A simulated tool-sorting task demonstrates how VABAR evaluates robot manipulation skills for industrial workflows. Agents Turn Skills Into Robot Programs Successful task completion requires robots to coordinate multiple skills and adapt when something goes wrong. Building reliable programs for these multistep tasks remains a challenge. Agentic robotics helps solve that challenge. UC Berkeley’s new Graph-as-Policy (GaP) framework uses agents to connect individual skills into robot programs. Agents test these programs using NVIDIA Isaac open simulation technologies and refine them based on failures. This helps researchers scale development with less data while keeping the programs interpretable for engineers to review and verify before deployment. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/wipe-the-bar.mp4 GaP uses agents and simulation to turn individual robot skills into coordinated actions, such as wiping a bar. “To me, agentic robotics is the most exciting technological development since the internet in 1995,” said Ken Goldberg, professor of robotics at UC Berkeley and a lead on the VABAR and GaP projects. Ambi Robotics is exploring GaP for industrial automation. Ambi Robotics , Bosch Research and Siemens are all exploring GaP for its agentic robotics workflows across diverse industrial scenarios. Learn more by joining NVIDIA at CoRL . Ambi Robotics is exploring GaP for industrial automation. Ambi Robotics , Bosch Research and Siemens are all exploring GaP for its agentic robotics workflows across diverse industrial scenarios. Learn more by joining NVIDIA at CoRL .

title: Pensacola Felon Indicted on Federal Firearm Charge
body: Press Release Pensacola Felon Indicted on Federal Firearm Charge Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Florida Pensacola, Florida – Jeremy Olds, 39, of Pensacola, Florida, has been indicted in federal court for possessing a firearm as a convicted felon. John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida, announced the charge. Olds appeared before U.S. Magistrate Judge Hope T. Cannon for his arraignment at the United States Courthouse in Pensacola, Florida. Trial is set for December 14, 2026, at 8:00 a.m. before U.S. District Judge M. Casey Rodgers. If convicted, Olds faces up to 15 years in prison, three years of supervised release, and a $250,000 fine. The case is being investigated by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Brooke D. Lindsay. Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities . An indictment is merely an allegation by a grand jury that a defendant has committed a violation of federal criminal law; it is not evidence of guilt. All defendants are presumed innocent and entitled to a fair trial, during which the government bears the burden of proving guilt beyond a reasonable doubt. The United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida is one of 94 offices that serve as the nation’s principal litigators under the direction of the Attorney General. To access public court documents online, please visit the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida website.  For more information about the United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida, visit https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndfl . title: Miramar Beach Man Forfeits Foreign Antiquities to United States
body: Press Release Miramar Beach Man Forfeits Foreign Antiquities to United States Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Florida Pensacola, Florida – Matthew Weinberg, of Miramar Beach, Florida, forfeited to the United States multiple antiquities dating as far back as circa 3000 BC. The seizure and forfeiture was announced by John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida. U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “Thanks to the hard work of my tenacious attorneys, these improperly obtained foreign antiquities have been recovered and will be repatriated back to their countries of origin. Special thanks go to our federal law enforcement partners for investigating these violations of our anti-smuggling statutes, and for ensuring these ancient artifacts are returned to their rightful owners.” Court documents reveal that in July 2025, agents from Homeland Security Investigations were notified by the U.S. Customs and Border Protection Office in Pensacola, Florida, regarding the detention of a shipment inbound to Pensacola International Airport from the United Arab Emirates. The shipment was detained but was destined for Weinberg. The manifest for the shipment claimed it contained two terracotta objects valued at less than $200 but, in truth, upon appraisal after detention, it contained two cuneiform tablets valued at over $15,000 in total that date back to 3000-2000 BC from modern day Iraq. Multiple other shipments to Weinberg were then investigated, and it was determined that he obtained shipments, contrary to law, from Iran, Egypt, and Cyprus as well. All of these shipments were significantly undervalued on their manifests just as were the tablets from Iraq. These shipments included bronze figures, ceramic architectural models, and terracotta idols. In March 2026, federal agents executed a search and seizure warrant on Weinberg’s residence in Miramar Beach. Seized from his residence were, amongst other things, ancient Hebrew Torah scrolls, scroll artwork originating from China, and items from circa 712-525 BC Egypt. Below are sample images of some of the items seized from Weinberg by the Department of Homeland Security: Due to import restrictions agreed upon by the United States and Iraq, Egypt, Cyprus, and other countries, Weinberg was prohibited from the possession of these artifacts. In addition to forfeiting the artifacts to the United States for repatriation back to their countries of origin, Weinberg forfeited $75,000 in United States currency as proceeds of violations of federal anti-smuggling statutes. He will also be barred for two years from selling or purchasing any foreign antiquities or artifacts. The case was investigated by Homeland Security Investigations and U.S. Customs and Border Protection in Pensacola, Florida. The case was handled by Assistant United States Attorneys Winifred L. Acosta and David L. Goldberg. The United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida is one of 94 offices that serve as the nation’s principal litigators under the direction of the Attorney General.  To access public court documents online, please visit the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida website. For more information about the United States Attorney’s Office, Northern District of Florida, visit https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndfl . title: Columbia County Man Pleads Guilty to Unlawful Firearm Dealing to Mexico
body: Press Release Columbia County Man Pleads Guilty to Unlawful Firearm Dealing to Mexico Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Florida Gainesville, Florida – Jose Manuel Barron, 32, of Columbia County, Florida, has pleaded guilty in federal court on a charge of conspiracy to transfer firearms to a nonresident and making false statements to a firearms dealer. John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida announced the guilty plea. According to court records, between June 2019 and February 2022, the defendant agreed to transfer, sell, and deliver multiple firearms to an intended recipient in Mexico. These firearms were all military style assault weapons, including two Barrett .50 BMG caliber rifles, a Colt 5.56 caliber rifle, and a Model M240 SLR 7.62 caliber rifle. Barron acquired one of the firearms under false pretenses from a federal firearms dealer. Three of the firearms were later recovered in Culiacan, Sinaloa, Mexico. Sentencing is scheduled for January 26, 2027, at 3:00pm before Chief United States District Court Judge Allen C. Winsor in Gainesville, Florida. The defendant faces up to five years of imprisonment. The case was investigated by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Adam Hapner. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities . body: Press Release Quincy Felon Pleads Guilty to Gun Possession Monday, November 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Florida Tallahassee, Florida – Eric Felton Cooper Jr., 36, of Quincy, Florida, has pleaded guilty in federal court to possession of a firearm by a convicted felon. John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida announced the plea. U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “Our brave men and women of law enforcement are fighting hard every day to keep our communities safe from dangerous criminals, like this defendant, and my office is prepared to aggressively prosecute these cases to hold those individuals accountable to the fullest extent of the law.” On January 18, 2026, law enforcement responded to a 911 call involving a firearm. While on scene, law enforcement learned that the defendant armed himself with a firearm during an argument with another individual. At the time that the defendant possessed the firearm, he was a convicted felon and could not legally possess a firearm. Cooper now faces up to 15 years’ imprisonment. Sentencing is scheduled for January 15, 2027, at 11:00 am before District Court Judge Mark E. Walker in Tallahassee, Florida. title: NVIDIA Announces New Planned Investments in Korean Startups at the MSIT-NVIDIA AI Startup Partnership Forum
body: NVIDIA Announces New Planned Investments in Korean Startups at the MSIT-NVIDIA AI Startup Partnership Forum November 9, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT and NVIDIA hosted the MSIT -NVIDIA AI Startup Partnership Forum at COEX. Ryu Je-myung, vice minister of science and ICT , joined NVIDIA leaders to meet with over 20 Korean startups across foundation models, physical AI, AI infrastructure and AI semiconductors. NVIDIA also announced an investment in Korean startup Point2 , with additional investments planned in Motif Technologies , RLWRLD and Upstage. Point2 Technology, an AI interconnect company, builds scalable, radio frequency-based interconnects that move data between chips and racks in AI factories, offering an innovative alternative to conventional copper and optical interconnect solutions for AI cluster scale-up, delivering the reach, performance and efficiency needed for next-generation AI infrastructure. Motif Technologies , a Seoul-based AI lab, develops foundation models for building AI agents that carry out complex tasks, including Motif-3, a large language model released with open weights. RLWRLD, a physical AI startup based in San Francisco, Seoul and Tokyo, develops robotics foundation models that enable humanoid and industrial robots to perform complex real-world tasks that require five-finger dexterity, such as precisely inserting components, threading nuts onto bolts and kitting parts from moving conveyors. Upstage , a Korean enterprise AI company, develops Solar language models and document AI tools that help businesses extract information from complex documents, streamline workflows and build AI applications for everyday operations. The companies represent work across the full AI stack , from infrastructure to models to robotics applications. The planned investments build on NVIDIA’s work with Korea’s startup and venture community, including more than 1,000 Korea-based members of NVIDIA Inception , a program that helps startups grow with access to preferred pricing, technical expertise and opportunities for investor introductions. title: Korea Advances Physical AI Across Industries With NVIDIA
body: Korea Advances Physical AI Across Industries With NVIDIA November 8, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Tapping into the country’s strengths in manufacturing and engineering, NVIDIA is helping advance Korea’s physical AI ecosystem. The country’s industry leaders are applying accelerated computing, AI and simulation to everything from semiconductor manufacturing to robotics and autonomous vehicles. These efforts are helping bring physical AI from development into real-world production. Samsung Advances Semiconductor Engineering With Accelerated Computing and AI Physics Samsung Electronics is expanding its collaboration with NVIDIA to advance semiconductor innovation through accelerated computing and AI physics. The work spans materials research, process development and device engineering. In technology computer-aided design, Samsung is working with NVIDIA cuISS and NVIDIA cuDSS to accelerate computations involving sparse linear systems. The collaboration also extends to GPU acceleration for process and optical simulations. In materials research, Samsung’s sMOL platform has run selected quantum chemical calculations up to 5x faster end to end with NVIDIA cuEST . Samsung is also exploring NVIDIA cuEquivariance to speed up tensor operations used in training and inference for atomistic AI models. Samsung is developing chip-scale thermal and mechanical analysis workflows with NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo . In one AI homogenization case, combining AI-predicted effective material properties, coarser grids and GPU acceleration resulted in a roughly 1,600x speedup. Simulation time fell from about 18 hours for a fine-grid solve on a 32-core CPU to 41 seconds for a GPU-accelerated coarse-grid solve. Looking ahead, NVIDIA Agent Toolkit could connect these simulation tools and AI models, helping future engineering agents run analyses and compare design options. Kakao Mobility Collaborates With NVIDIA to Advance Autonomous Driving Development Kakao Mobility plans to build on NVIDIA’s autonomous vehicle computing and safety technologies to advance development of a level 4 autonomous driving system. The work combines Kakao Mobility’s proprietary driving software and experience operating in Seoul’s Gangnam district with NVIDIA’s vehicle computing platform. Kakao Mobility plans to use NVIDIA Hyperion , a reference platform for vehicle sensors and compute, powered by NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor. It also plans to use NVIDIA Halos to support safety across the development and validation of its autonomous driving technology. Initial development is planned around Kia purpose-built vehicles, integrating Kakao Mobility’s autonomous driving software with NVIDIA technologies. The effort aims to support future level 4 mobility services in Korea. LG Electronics Advances Robot Learning and Factory Simulation NVIDIA and LG Electronics successfully demonstrated NVIDIA Isaac GR00T-powered robotic manipulation and manufacturing tasks using LG’s CLOiD robot in an actual manufacturing environment. The collaboration implemented a physical AI data flywheel connecting real-world data collection, NVIDIA Cosmos-based data augmentation, GR00T model training, NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor onboard computing and simulation-based evaluation, establishing reusable workflows for continued development and validation of CLOiD’s robotic capabilities. The teams are using this work to refine a repeatable process for training, evaluating and improving robots for manufacturing. title: Korea’s AI Ecosystem Advances and Secures Agentic AI With NVIDIA
body: Korea’s AI Ecosystem Advances and Secures Agentic AI With NVIDIA Hyundai Motor Group and AIM Intelligence explore NVIDIA NemoClaw and OpenShell for secure enterprise agents, and LG AI Research opens API for ‘K-EXAONE-2.5’ trained on Nemotron datasets. November 8, 2026 by Nicola Sessions 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! As AI agents take on more work, they need capable open models and security that advances alongside them. Hyundai Motor Group is exploring NVIDIA NemoClaw blueprints and the NVIDIA OpenShell runtime, while AIM Intelligence is integrating its Starfort platform with NVIDIA OpenShell to support secure AI agents for employee productivity and enterprise workflows . A key component of the NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform, OpenShell provides a secure runtime with sandboxed execution and policy-based controls to safeguard sensitive data, manage access to enterprise tools and govern autonomous agent actions. AIM Intelligence , a Korean AI security company, is integrating its Starfort agent control platform with NVIDIA OpenShell. The goal is to combine OpenShell’s runtime access controls with Starfort’s detection of malicious instructions and data leakage. The company is also considering a preliminary proof of concept for the public energy sector, with potential applications across enterprise, industrial and robotics environments. On the model side, LG AI Research is opening application programming interface access for K-EXAONE-2.5, developed using NVIDIA Nemotron datasets, including Nemotron-Personas-Korea . Nemotron-Personas-Korea is an open dataset of 7 million fully synthetic Korean personas, grounded in official Korean statistics, that model builders use to ground training data and evaluation in Korean contexts. NVIDIA Nemotron is a family of open models, datasets and techniques that help developers build specialized, efficient AI agents. Learn more about NVIDIA Nemotron open models and get started building secure agents with NVIDIA OpenShell . title: From Chips to Skills, NVIDIA and Korea Expand Sovereign AI Collaboration
body: From Chips to Skills, NVIDIA and Korea Expand Sovereign AI Collaboration November 8, 2026 by Jesse Clayton 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA and Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT) are expanding their collaboration across the country’s sovereign AI ecosystem, from AI semiconductors and data center infrastructure to talent, startups, models, agents and security. The collaboration lays the groundwork for Korean NPU and XPU companies to explore participation in the NVIDIA NVLink Fusion ecosystem, and includes NVIDIA training and certification programs, hackathons and technical seminars to strengthen GPU utilization. Through Korea’s AI for All initiative, NVIDIA will collaborate with three selected consortia and four leading Korean foundation model builders, using NVIDIA Dynamo software to optimize and scale AI inference. In addition, NVIDIA today announced a collaboration with SK Telecom and Rebellions, supported by MSIT, to advance sovereign AI infrastructure for Korean models and workloads with NVIDIA NVLink Fusion. Read more in the press release . title: NVIDIA Dynamo Recipes Bring Korea’s Leading Open Models to Production
body: NVIDIA Dynamo Recipes Bring Korea’s Leading Open Models to Production November 8, 2026 by Amr Elmeleegy 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA is releasing Dynamo-optimized deployment recipes for Korea’s leading open models: A.X K2 from SK Telecom , K-EXAONE 2.0 from LG AI Research , Solar Open 2 from Upstage and Motif-3 from Motif Technologies . As models grow beyond the capacity of a single GPU, they must be split across multiple GPUs, requiring careful coordination of request routing and communication to maintain performance. NVIDIA Dynamo is an open source, distributed inference-serving framework built to deploy models in multi-node environments at data center scale. It handles this routing and communication to maximize inference performance. Optimized for NVIDIA B200 GPUs, these recipes take the guesswork out of deployment, delivering up to 2x performance out of the box. They help developers bring Korea’s open models into production faster and turn them into broadly accessible AI for All services. Learn more about NVIDIA Dynamo .
